title: Prism: first install
summary: PhotoPrism on the lab box with Docker Compose, LAN only: index a folder you already have and open it from your phone. Mark installed when it works.

start.body:
Prism here means PhotoPrism: a photo library you run that browses and searches folders you already have. It starts lighter than Immich, with one app container and one database.

This walkthrough gets it running on the lab box, on your home network only.

fit.body: It suits you if your photos already live in folders and you want to browse and search them from any screen in the house. Face clustering and automatic phone backup can wait.

choices.label: I already run it — mark Prism and photos installed

prereq.body: You need Docker with Compose on the lab box, about 4 GB of RAM plus 4 GB of swap, and the box reachable on your home network. SSH in from the couch for the commands that follow.

need-docker.body:
Install Docker Engine from the official Docker docs for your OS, then check it:

```
docker compose version
```

Come back when that prints a version.

folder.body: Pick the folder PhotoPrism will read, for example /srv/photos. It indexes your photos where they are and does not move them, so keep that folder on a disk with room and a backup.

download.body:
Make a folder for PhotoPrism and download its official Compose file:

```
mkdir -p ~/photoprism && cd ~/photoprism
wget https://dl.photoprism.app/docker/compose.yaml
```

edit.body:
Open the file:

```
nano compose.yaml
```

Set PHOTOPRISM_ADMIN_PASSWORD to a long password (8 characters minimum). Change the database password too: MARIADB_PASSWORD and PHOTOPRISM_DATABASE_PASSWORD must match. Under volumes, change "~/Pictures:/photoprism/originals" so the left side is your photo folder. Do this before the first start; these passwords cannot be changed in this file afterwards.

up.body:
Start it and check both containers are running:

```
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
```

The first start can take a minute.

web.body: On a laptop on house Wi-Fi, open http://lab-address:2342 and sign in as admin with the password you set. Keep it on your home network: no port forwarding.

index.body: In PhotoPrism, open Library, then Index, and start indexing. A big folder takes a while; thumbnails fill in as it goes.

empty.body:
An empty library usually means the originals path is wrong. Check what PhotoPrism sees:

```
docker compose exec photoprism ls /photoprism/originals
```

If your folders are missing, fix the volumes line in compose.yaml, run docker compose up -d again, and index again.

phone.body: On your phone, on house Wi-Fi, open http://lab-address:2342 in the browser and sign in. You can add it to the home screen. Try the Upload button with a couple of photos and watch them appear in the library.

choices.label: It works — mark Prism and photos installed
Still wrestling — keep Prism as interested

stuck.body: Usual causes: the wrong lab address, the containers not running (docker compose ps), or the lab box's firewall blocking port 2342 from your home network. Replay this walkthrough when you are ready.

interested.body: Noted. Replay this walkthrough when you have an evening. Keep it on your home network until you know how you would sign in from outside.

installed.body: Good. Keep a second copy of the photo folder off the box — same rule as any photo pile.

skip.body: Fine. Immich or plain folder backup still cover most houses.
